instruction.name: xvldrepl.d
instruction.description: Read 64-bit data from memory address `addr + offset`, replicate the data to all vector lanes and save into `dst`. Address misalignment does not raise an exception. The `offset` operand is a byte offset, matching the assembly immediate; the encoded instruction stores it as a scaled immediate for wider elements.

throughput.name: 8 independent lanes
throughput.asm: xvldrepl.d $xr0, $r20, 0; xvldrepl.d $xr1, $r20, 8; xvldrepl.d $xr2, $r20, 16; xvldrepl.d $xr3, $r20, 24; xvldrepl.d $xr4, $r20, 32; xvldrepl.d $xr5, $r20, 40; xvldrepl.d $xr6, $r20, 48; xvldrepl.d $xr7, $r20, 56
throughput.command: ./bench --unroll 1000 --iters 1000 --warmup 10 --reps 5 --core 0 --init 'addi.d $r20, $sp, -1024; li.d $r4, -64; and $r20, $r20, $r4' --asm 'xvldrepl.d $xr0, $r20, 0; xvldrepl.d $xr1, $r20, 8; xvldrepl.d $xr2, $r20, 16; xvldrepl.d $xr3, $r20, 24; xvldrepl.d $xr4, $r20, 32; xvldrepl.d $xr5, $r20, 40; xvldrepl.d $xr6, $r20, 48; xvldrepl.d $xr7, $r20, 56'

notes: No destination data dependency; latency is not defined. Throughput only.
